content_list.content_text: When Parasite (2019) won the Oscar for Best Picture on February 9, 2020, many treated the victory as a happy accident, the kind of exception that only proves the rule. There was reason for doubt: it had taken 92 ceremonies for a non-English-language film to win the top prize, and nothing guaranteed that the next one wouldn't put everything back to normal. A month later, the pandemic shut down movie theaters around the world, and the question hung in the air: would the door opened by Bong Joon Ho stay open? The answer came gradually, from different places and not always via the Academy's stage, but it came. In the years that followed, films from Korea, Japan, India, Europe and China showed that Parasite had not been a fluke. And at the end of the road stood Brazil.

information.contentText: A scene from Bong Joon Ho's film, the first in a language other than English to win the Oscar for Best Picture, in February 2020.

content_list.content_text: The following year brought a curious case. Minari (2021), directed by Lee Isaac Chung, is an American production, made by the son of Korean immigrants and spoken mostly in Korean. As a result, the Golden Globes placed it in the foreign-language film category, out of the running for Best Picture, a widely criticized decision. At the Oscars on April 25, 2021, Youn Yuh-jung, playing the grandmother who comes from Korea to live with the family in Arkansas, won Best Supporting Actress and became the first Korean actress honored by the Academy. In 2022, it was Japan's turn. Drive My Car (2021), directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi, a three-hour drama based on a Haruki Murakami short story (the opening credits don't appear until about 40 minutes in), received four nominations, including Best Picture, a first for a Japanese film, and won the Oscar for International Feature.

On March 12, 2023, the night belonged to Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022). An American A24 production directed by the duo Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert and starring a predominantly Asian cast, the multiverse comedy about a Chinese immigrant who owns a laundromat won seven Oscars, including Best Picture. Michelle Yeoh became the first Asian woman to win Best Actress, and Ke Huy Quan, the kid from Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom who had spent nearly two decades away from the camera, took Supporting Actor. At the same ceremony, Germany's Im Westen nichts Neues (All Quiet on the Western Front, 2022), directed by Edward Berger, won four statuettes (International Feature, Cinematography, Original Score and Production Design) and showed that Netflix had gotten the message: a war film in German could also be a global product.

content_list.title: Why Everything Everywhere All At Once Hits So Hard
content_list.description: Thomas Flight explores why the multiverse chaos of the Daniels' film, packed with absurd gags and parallel universes, manages to end in such a moving story about family and love.

content_list.content_text: India reached the stage through a side door. The country did not pick RRR (2022) as its official submission (the slot went to the Gujarati-language drama Chhello Show), so director S. S. Rajamouli and his team mounted an independent campaign in the United States. It paid off: the Telugu-language epic about two revolutionaries who take on British rule had already become a phenomenon on Netflix, where it spent weeks among the most-watched films. The musical number “Naatu Naatu” won the Golden Globe and then the Oscar for Original Song, the first ever for a song from an Indian film. RRR also symbolizes a shift within India itself: released dubbed into several languages, it is a landmark of pan-Indian cinema, in which productions from the country's south, and no longer just Bollywood, dominate the national box office. In 2024, the top earner was Pushpa 2, also in Telugu.

information.contentText: Composer M. M. Keeravani and lyricist Chandrabose accept the 2023 Oscar for Original Song for the musical number from RRR, the Academy's first award for a song from an Indian film.

content_list.content_text: On March 10, 2024, Japan left the ceremony with two awards that said a lot about the new landscape. Godzilla Minus One (2023), directed by Takashi Yamazaki, cost less than $15 million, according to the director, a fraction of the budget of an American blockbuster, and still won the Oscar for Visual Effects over Hollywood productions. It was the franchise's first Oscar nomination in nearly 70 years, and the win made Yamazaki, who also supervised the effects, the first director to win in the category since Stanley Kubrick for 2001: A Space Odyssey. That same night, The Boy and the Heron (2023) gave Hayao Miyazaki his second Oscar for Animated Feature, more than 20 years after Spirited Away. A cheap monster and an 83-year-old master proved that Japanese cinema didn't need to imitate Hollywood to beat it.

content_list.title: RRR - The Biggest Blockbuster You've Never Heard Of
content_list.description: Patrick (H) Willems introduces RRR to viewers who only know Hollywood blockbusters and shows why S. S. Rajamouli's epic deserves to be discovered by American audiences.

content_list.content_text: The same 2024 ceremony had two European films among the ten Best Picture nominees. Anatomie d'une chute (Anatomy of a Fall, 2023), directed by Justine Triet and winner of the Palme d'Or at Cannes, wasn't even chosen by France to compete for International Feature (the country preferred The Taste of Things), but it made it into the main categories on its own and won Original Screenplay. The Zone of Interest (2023), directed by Jonathan Glazer, a British production spoken almost entirely in German, won International Feature and Sound with the story of the family of the Auschwitz commandant, who live next to the death camp as if nothing were happening. Germany's Sandra Hüller was in the lead cast of both. Four years after Parasite, non-English-language films were no longer exotic visitors in the top race: they were real contenders, judged by an Academy that had changed its face.

information.contentTitle: The visual effects of Godzilla Minus One
information.contentText: An official Toho video on the effects of Godzilla Minus One, made on a modest budget and honored with the 2024 Oscar, the first in the franchise's history.

content_list.content_text: That openness also brought a new kind of scrutiny, and the case of Emilia Pérez (2024) shows it. French director Jacques Audiard's musical, spoken almost entirely in Spanish and set in Mexico but shot on a soundstage near Paris, arrived at the 2025 Oscars with 13 nominations, a record for a non-English-language film. The campaign quickly fell apart. In Mexico, critics and relatives of the disappeared accused the film of treating drug trafficking and its victims with stereotypes and superficiality, and of lacking Mexican leads. Days after the nominations, old racist and Islamophobic posts by Karla Sofía Gascón, the first openly trans actress nominated for an Oscar, resurfaced, and Netflix sidelined her from the campaign. The film walked away with two awards: Supporting Actress, for Zoe Saldaña, and Original Song, for “El Mal.” The lesson was clear: at a more global Oscars, it also matters who tells whose story.

information.contentText: Zoe Saldaña in one of the musical numbers from Jacques Audiard's film. Of its 13 nominations, only two turned into statuettes: Supporting Actress, for her, and Original Song, for “El Mal.”

content_list.content_text: Far from the Academy's party, the shift showed up at the box office. Released on January 29, 2025, the first day of the Chinese New Year, Ne Zha 2 (2025), directed by Jiaozi, grossed about $2.27 billion, nearly all of it in China, becoming the highest-grossing animated film in history and the biggest hit ever for a non-English-language film. More than 4,000 professionals from 138 Chinese studios worked on it. Months later, Korean culture conquered the planet by another route: KPop Demon Hunters (2025), an American production from Sony Pictures Animation directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, about a K-pop group that hunts demons, premiered on Netflix in June and became the most-watched film in the platform's history. In March 2026, it won the Oscars for Animated Feature and Original Song, for “Golden.”

information.contentTitle: “Golden” wins the Oscar for Original Song
information.contentText: EJAE and the songwriters of KPop Demon Hunters accept the award in 2026. “Golden” was the first K-pop song honored by the Academy.

content_list.content_text: And then it was Brazil's turn. I'm Still Here (2024), directed by Walter Salles, adapts Marcelo Rubens Paiva's memoir about his mother, Eunice, who watched her husband, former congressman Rubens Paiva, be taken from their home by agents of Brazil's military dictatorship in January 1971, never to return. Awarded for its screenplay at the Venice Film Festival, the film opened in Brazilian theaters on November 7, 2024, and drew more than 5 million moviegoers, the largest audience for a Brazilian film since the pandemic. On January 5, 2025, Fernanda Torres won the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Drama, beating Nicole Kidman, Angelina Jolie and Kate Winslet, and became the first Brazilian to win in an acting category. There was something of a reckoning in it: more than 25 years earlier, her mother, Fernanda Montenegro, who appears in the film as the elderly Eunice, had been nominated for an Oscar for Central Station (1998), also directed by Walter Salles.

content_list.title: I'm Still Here: the memory that became a phenomenon
content_list.description: Marcelo Rubens Paiva's book, published in 2015, was written when his mother, Eunice, was already living with Alzheimer's, so it is also about memory slipping away. After her husband's disappearance, Eunice was jailed and interrogated for 12 days, raised their five children on her own, earned a law degree and became a leading advocate for Indigenous rights. Only in 1996, after a long battle she led, did the Brazilian state issue Rubens Paiva's death certificate. Walter Salles's film turned this family story into a national conversation, in the year the 1964 military coup marked its 60th anniversary. Calls for a boycott from the far right did not stop audiences from packing theaters. Reality kept pace with fiction: on January 23, 2025, the same day the film received its three Oscar nominations, the certificate was amended to record a death that was “unnatural, violent, caused by the Brazilian state.”

click.button_text: Read about the new death certificate

content_list.content_text: The Oscar ceremony, on March 2, 2025, fell on a Carnival Sunday, and Brazil watched as if it were a World Cup final. The film was competing in three categories, including Best Picture, the first nomination for an entirely Brazilian production in the top race. Fernanda Torres lost Best Actress to Mikey Madison of Anora, but when Penélope Cruz announced I'm Still Here as Best International Feature, the celebration spilled into the streets. At the Sambadrome in Rio and on the sound trucks of Salvador's Carnival, where singer Daniela Mercury shouted “dictatorship never again” into the microphone, revelers celebrated with replica statuettes and Fernanda Torres costumes. It was the first Oscar ever for a Brazilian production. Until then, the closest the country had come was Black Orpheus, which won in 1960 with a Brazilian cast but as France's entry.

quote.quote: This award goes to her, Eunice Paiva, and to the two extraordinary women who gave life to her: Fernanda Torres and Fernanda Montenegro.
quote.author: Walter Salles (Oscar acceptance speech, 2025)

content_list.content_text: The success was no isolated lightning strike. In May 2025, The Secret Agent (2025), directed by Kleber Mendonça Filho, a thriller set in Recife during the 1977 Carnival, at the height of the dictatorship, won the Best Director and Best Actor awards at Cannes, the latter for Wagner Moura, the first Brazilian to win Best Actor at the festival. Kleber, for his part, became the second Brazilian honored for directing at Cannes, after Glauber Rocha in 1969. In January 2026, the film won two Golden Globes (Non-English Language Film and Actor in a Drama) and soon after received four Oscar nominations: Best Picture, Actor, International Feature and Casting. Moura was the first Brazilian ever nominated for Best Actor. At the March 15, 2026, ceremony, however, the film went home empty-handed, beaten by Norway's Sentimental Value, by Michael B. Jordan for Sinners and by One Battle After Another. Even so, Brazil had reached the Best Picture race for the second year in a row.

information.contentText: Wagner Moura plays a hunted man in dictatorship-era Recife in Kleber Mendonça Filho's film, an award winner at Cannes and nominated for four Oscars in 2026.

content_list.content_text: What changed between Parasite and The Secret Agent? Partly, who votes: the Academy became more international and began to see with fresh eyes films that once reached American members only with a great deal of luck. Partly, how people watch: streaming made subtitles a habit, and titles like RRR and All Quiet on the Western Front found American audiences through Netflix. And, most important, what gets told: deeply local films, about a Korean family in Arkansas, two Indian revolutionaries against the British Empire or a Brazilian mother searching for her disappeared husband, proved they didn't need to water themselves down to speak to the world. Hollywood remains cinema's biggest stage, but it is no longer the only one. For Brazil, which celebrated an Oscar the way it celebrates a goal, the lesson was that its own memory, told with courage, can be universal.

content_list.title: An Academy without borders: how the voting body changed
content_list.description: Part of the explanation for the shift lies in the voter rolls. After #OscarsSoWhite in 2016, the Academy began inviting hundreds of new members each year, with far more women, people of color and professionals from outside the United States. The share of international members rose from 13% in 2016 to about 20% in 2019, and the Academy, which had roughly 6,000 members in 2016, tops 11,000 with the class of 2026. In the class of 2025, 55% of the 534 invitees came from outside the U.S., among them ten Brazilians, such as Fernanda Torres, director Daniela Thomas and the screenwriters of I'm Still Here, Murilo Hauser and Heitor Lorega. Wagner Moura had already been invited in 2021. In the class of 2026, 53% of the 529 invitees were from abroad. When Drive My Car was nominated for Best Picture, the American press linked the feat to this renewal. More voters from Seoul, Paris, Mumbai and São Paulo mean more people who watch a subtitled film without treating it as “foreign,” and campaigns that have to speak to the whole world.

movies.title: Parasita
movies.overview: Toda a família de Ki-taek está desempregada, vivendo num porão sujo e apertado. Uma obra do acaso faz com que o filho adolescente da família comece a dar aulas de inglês à garota de uma família rica. Fascinados com a vida luxuosa destas pessoas, pai, mãe, filho e filha bolam um plano para se infiltrarem também na família glamorosa, um a um. No entanto, os segredos e mentiras necessários à ascensão social custarão caro a todos.

movies.title: Minari: Em Busca da Felicidade
movies.overview: Uma família coreano-americana se muda para uma fazenda no Arkansas em busca de seu próprio sonho americano. Em meio aos desafios dessa nova vida, eles descobrem a inegável resiliência da família e o que realmente faz um lar.

movies.original_title: ドライブ・マイ・カー
movies.title: Drive My Car
movies.overview: Dois anos após a morte de sua esposa, Yusuke Kafuku recebe uma oferta para dirigir uma peça num festival de teatro em Hiroshima. Lá, ele conhece Misaki, uma jovem reservada, designada para ser sua motorista. Enquanto passam tempo juntos, Kafuku confronta o mistério de sua esposa que o assombra.

movies.title: Tudo em Todo o Lugar ao Mesmo Tempo
movies.overview: Uma imigrante chinesa parte rumo a uma aventura onde, sozinha, precisará salvar o mundo, explorando outros universos e outras vidas que poderia ter vivido. Contudo, as coisas se complicam quando ela fica presa nessa infinidade de possibilidades sem conseguir retornar para casa.

movies.title: Nada de Novo no Front
movies.overview: Convocado para a linha de frente da Primeira Guerra Mundial, o adolescente Paul encara a dura realidade da vida nas trincheiras.

movies.title: RRR: Revolta, Rebelião, Revolução
movies.overview: Um guerreiro corajoso em uma missão perigosa encontra um policial durão que serve ao exército britânico nesta saga épica ambientada na Índia pré-independência.

movies.title: Godzilla Minus One
movies.overview: Em um Japão social e economicamente devastado após o término da Segunda Guerra Mundial, a situação chega a um nível ainda mais crítico quando uma gigantesca e misteriosa criatura surge do mar para assolar o país.

movies.original_title: 君たちはどう生きるか
movies.title: O Menino e a Garça
movies.overview: Depois de perder a mãe durante a guerra, o jovem Mahito muda-se para a propriedade de sua família no campo. Lá, uma série de eventos misteriosos o levam a uma torre antiga e isolada, lar de uma travessa garça cinzenta. Quando a nova madrasta de Mahito desaparece, ele segue a garça até a torre e entra num mundo fantástico partilhado pelos vivos e pelos mortos. Ao embarcar em uma jornada épica com a garça como guia, Mahito deve descobrir os segredos deste mundo e a verdade sobre si mesmo.

movies.title: Anatomia de uma Queda
movies.overview: Uma mulher é suspeita do assassinato de seu marido, e seu filho cego enfrenta um dilema moral como única testemunha.

movies.title: Zona de Interesse
movies.overview: O comandante Rudolf Höss e sua esposa Hedwig, desfrutam de uma vida aparentemente comum em uma casa com um belo jardim. Mas, por trás da fachada de tranquilidade, a família feliz vive, na verdade, ao lado do campo de concentração de Auschwitz. O dia-a dia destes personagens se desenrola entre os gritos abafados de desespero de um genocídio do qual eles tem as mãos manchadas de sangue.

movies.title: Ne Zha 2: O Renascer da Alma
movies.overview: Após uma grande catástrofe, as almas de Ne Zha e Ao Bing são salvas, mas seus corpos enfrentam a ruína. Para lhes dar uma nova vida, Taiyi Zhenren recorre à mística lótus de sete cores em uma ousada tentativa de reconstruí-los e mudar seus destinos.

movies.title: Guerreiras do K-Pop
movies.overview: Quando não estão lotando estádios, as estrelas do K-pop Rumi, Mira e Zoey usam seus poderes secretos para proteger os fãs contra ameaças sobrenaturais.

movies.title: Ainda Estou Aqui
movies.overview: No início da década de 1970, o Brasil enfrenta o endurecimento da ditadura militar. No Rio de Janeiro, a família Paiva – Rubens, Eunice e seus cinco filhos – vive à beira da praia em uma casa de portas abertas para os amigos. Um dia, Rubens Paiva é levado por militares à paisana e desaparece.

movies.title: O Agente Secreto
movies.overview: No Brasil de 1977, Marcelo, um especialista em tecnologia fugindo de um passado misterioso, volta ao Recife em busca de um pouco de paz, mas percebe que a cidade está longe de ser o refúgio que procura.

content_list.subtitle: The events that shaped the world
content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 2020 to Today
content_list.description: The pandemic shuts down theaters, streaming consolidates, Hollywood grinds to a halt with strikes and world cinema rises to the top. Click here to see the main events in cinema from 2020 to today in chronological order.
